cards.front: Classifying proximal femur fractures is easier if the patient is placed in traction with internal rotation positioning.
cards.extra: Koval et al (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18537778/) performed a study in which proximal femur fractures were classified with standard radiographs (AP pelvis, AP hip, cross-table lateral), followed by the addition of a physician-assisted view with traction and 15 degrees of internal rotation. The inclusion of the traction-internal rotation view led to increased agreement in classification between the authors, and was especially helpful for differentiating displaced femoral neck fractures versus stable intertrochanteric fractures.
